body:
The three positions disagree less about the facts than about what a written record would be for, and that turns out to be the productive question. The account treats a record as a memory prosthetic: capture what was agreed so it cannot drift. The rival argues a note like 'A: dishes, Mon' is not self-interpreting. The objection argues a record cannot settle what 'done' or 'this week' should mean once schedules shift. Read together, these are not rival verdicts on one artifact; they are correct claims about three different artifacts. A record of words captures only what was said, and helps only if the loss was memorial. A record of explicit terms — task, person, window, what 'done' includes, whether it recurs — helps only if the divergence was in content at the moment of agreement. Neither settles how an agreement should adapt when schedules change; that needs a third element, a renegotiation trigger: an expiry and a re-agree point tied to the schedule changes themselves. And under the rival's third reading, no version of the record touches the problem — it relocates the argument onto who wrote it, who is on it, who is keeping score.

That unification decides some things for me. I am revising the account's central conjecture rather than keeping or dropping it whole. 'We later disagree about what the agreement meant' does not decide between meaning that was shared and then lost, and meaning that was never shared — both parties can sincerely have agreed to different things at the moment of speaking, as the rival says. The material's own phrasing — agreement on who survives while the meaning fails — fits both: differential forgetting is normal memory behavior, and so is sincere divergence. So the memory-gap reading becomes a disjunction, shared-then-lost or never-formed, and the practical consequence is amended: if any record is kept, it must capture explicit terms at the moment of agreement, not a transcript of loose words afterwards. The account's slide from 'no shared record' to 'make a shared record' was too fast, as the rival says; the repaired move is 'make disambiguation the point of the record.'

I am rejecting the account's proposed test as it stood. The objection's criticism is sound: watching whether 'what was agreed' disputes fall can read either outcome as support. The rival's probe replaces it, and I am taking that probe as the first move: ask each flatmate separately what they took a recent disputed agreement to mean — task, recurrence, timing, what counted as done — explicitly not to adjudicate. Running it before any intervention is what lets its output discriminate. I want the interpretation map pre-registered now, before anyone runs anything, because that discipline is what the original test lacked: if disputes cluster around scope, recurrence or timing, a terms-record is apt; if both parties report the same terms but argue about fairness now that schedules have moved, the problem is adaptation, and renegotiation triggers are apt; if accounts do not cluster, or the disputes turn out to be about score-keeping and tone rather than terms, the rival's standing-negotiation reading gains weight and a record would likely just relocate the argument.

I am partially rejecting the rival's characterization of the account, on grounds available in the text: the account did not present the one-to-one approach as clearly correct — it flagged that move as the part it most wanted treated as contestable, and required curiosity rather than retrieval as its basis. What survives from the rival is the substantive worry: if the friend's avoidance comes from feeling outnumbered in the group, a private conversation about their withdrawal can reproduce that dynamic at smaller scale. That worry is a design constraint, not a veto. The approach should be folded into the probe — the friend is one of the 'each flatmate separately' — so the first one-to-one contact is about what agreements meant, not about their avoidance. If even that is declined, the refusal is itself the finding.

I am also declining the objection's reversal, while accepting most of its criticism. The objection is right that the account demoted avoidance to symptom on grounds the material does not supply, and right that the account's own dependency — assuming three people can talk without a mediator — is not a peripheral caveat. But the counter-ordering, making the avoidance the named first topic, is no better supported than the ordering it criticizes, and it runs straight into the dynamic the rival identified: the person who withdrew becomes the subject of the first conversation. The probe is the conservative option that does not require deciding that question first — it establishes one-to-one contact with the avoiding friend on a non-accusatory errand, and how that goes is evidence either way. What I keep from the objection: the memorial-versus-normative distinction, the weak-test criticism, and the dependency point — which now does work. If the probe is refused even one-to-one, a mediator moves from unnameable to nameable. Naming that trigger is not ranking mediators against other routes; I still have no basis to rank.

Two further decisions. First, everything proposed so far has quietly assumed household-level adoption, but the person asking is one flatmate. The probe is executable by one person; the record is not — it exists only if all three take it up, and the manner of its proposal is part of the intervention. A system presented by one member to two others is a different object than a habit the group adopts. Second, I am not carrying the weekly check-in forward as a default. Whether the failed thing was the topic (chores) or the format (unstructured argument) is unknown, and a scheduled meeting about chores is a bet on format-change that the avoiding friend experiences as a calendar entry. If a recurring conversation is later wanted, its function should be the renegotiation trigger — the scheduled place where terms are re-made when schedules shift — not a chore-court.

What would count against this: if the probe returns clean clusters, a terms-record is adopted, and the disputes persist at the same intensity, my sequencing was wrong — the rival's group-level conversation should have come first, and readings that treat the arguments as doing something other than failing to coordinate get stronger. If the friend accepts the probe but the group still cannot convene afterwards, the probe built no bridge, and the problem is not chore mechanics. A quiet week after any record remains uninformative, and I will not read it as success.

Still open, on the material's silence: which reading is true; whether the avoidance predates the schedule changes; whether anyone carries a heavier baseline load; whether the household wants formalization at all; and whether the friend's avoidance is about the chores at all. I hold those as gaps rather than filling them.
commitments:
Taking this up involves the following separable pieces.

The unification itself is a claim I am committing to: that the account, objection and rival are giving correct verdicts about three different artifacts — a record of words, a record of explicit terms, and terms plus renegotiation triggers — rather than disagreeing about one thing. It could be wrong: someone might show that in practice households do not distinguish recording words from recording terms, in which case the synthesis loses its organizing force and the inputs revert to being genuine rivals.

I am committing to the revised conjecture as a disjunction — shared-then-lost or never-formed meaning — and to its consequence: any record must capture explicit terms at the moment of agreement, not words after the fact. That consequence is conditional on a record being adopted at all; it is not a commitment that one should be.

The probe as first move is a proposal, executable by the asker alone. Taking it up means accepting its testimonial limits — it yields what people now say they took an agreement to mean, not what actually happened — and accepting that being asked may itself read as interrogation. I am committing to the pre-registered interpretation map as the discipline that replaces the rejected test, and, with the rival, to treating non-clustering answers as genuinely ambiguous rather than as confirmation of whichever reading the asker already favored. The map can mis-sort: a household whose real problem is standing could land in the 'terms' branch, and only persistent disputes after a terms-record would reveal the mis-sort.

Rejecting the account's original test is a commitment with stated grounds — the objection showed both outcomes readable as support. Anyone keeping the original test should say why that problem does not apply.

Partially rejecting the rival's characterization of the account is a textual commitment: the account's text flags the one-to-one move as most contestable and demands curiosity-framing, so 'presents it as clearly correct' is not accurate. The rival's substantive worry — the outnumbered dynamic — is adopted as a design constraint: the first one-to-one contact with the friend is the probe, not a conversation about their avoidance. Anyone who goes directly to 'why do you avoid the conversations' has dropped that constraint, and I would want the result counted that way.

Declining the objection's reversal while keeping its criticisms commits me to a sequencing claim: that establishing contact via the probe does not require first deciding whether avoidance is symptom or cause. This can fail in the direction the objection predicts — if avoidance is the mechanism, even a low-stakes errand may be experienced as the conversation resuming, and a refusal should then count as evidence for the objection's reading rather than as the friend being difficult.

Demoting the weekly check-in from default to conditional commits me to the view that we do not know whether the failed thing was topic or format. If a household adopts a check-in anyway, I am committed to reading its manner of proposal and its function — renegotiation trigger, not chore-court — as part of the intervention, not neutral delivery. Likewise the record: its introduction is itself a test, since under the standing reading the fight over who wrote it would be the signature.

The mediator remains unendorsed but acquires a trigger: refused one-to-one probe contact. Naming the trigger is not ranking mediators against other routes; I have no basis to rank, and a taker of this contribution inherits that inability rather than a hidden preference.

Failure commitments, stated in advance: if the probe clusters cleanly, a terms-record is adopted, and disputes persist at the same intensity, my sequencing was wrong and the group-level conversation should have come first — I would want that recorded against this contribution, not explained as the household doing it badly. If the friend accepts the probe but the group still cannot convene, the problem is not chore mechanics and this plan built no bridge. A quiet week remains uninformative in either direction.

Unresolved and not papered over: which reading is true; whether the avoidance predates the schedule changes; baseline load distribution; whether the household wants formalization; whether the avoidance is about chores at all. Any of these being filled could re-rank everything above, and taking this up means revising under that information rather than defending the sequence against it.
